title: Mutability and Constant
definition: Mutability permits state to change after initialization, while a constant binding prevents a defined class of reassignment.
purpose: Limit avoidable state changes and make intended change explicit.
history: Modern languages provide different binding and value mutability mechanisms to balance controlled change with expressiveness.
mental_model: A constant binding locks which value identity a name refers to; it does not necessarily freeze the internal state of a referenced object.
analogy: A fixed address label may point to a house whose contents change; the analogy fails because primitive values and object references have language-specific semantics.
common_mistakes: Assuming const makes an object immutable
Using mutable state without a real transition requirement
Replacing meaningful snapshots with one repeatedly reused variable
industry_notes: Defaulting to the narrowest mutation authority improves local reasoning, but immutable copying also has cost and must match the domain.
ai_notes: Ask AI to justify every mutable binding and provide a version with reduced mutation, then compare behavior and readability.
interview_notes: Ask why const prevents reassignment but not object property mutation in JavaScript.
exercise_candidates: Classify bindings as constant or mutable and defend each choice
lab_candidates: Reduce mutation while preserving account behavior
project_candidates: Document state ownership and transition points
